settings.title: Amazon basin
settings.text: A first-aid staple for centuries - indigenous communities applied the sap directly to cuts, burns and irritated skin as a protective "second skin".

settings.title: Ancient world
settings.text: Traded across the Mediterranean and Arabia as a precious dye, incense and remedy.

settings.title: Traditional Chinese practice
settings.text: Known as lóng xuè jié, used for centuries in southern China to support healing.

settings.title: Today
settings.text: Dermatology and cosmetic science are validating what traditional use already suggested - and isolating the compounds behind it.

settings.title: Proanthocyanidins
settings.text: The majority of the resin's dry weight. Potent antioxidants that help neutralise the free radicals generated by UV exposure, pollution and everyday environmental stress - the kind of damage that shows up over time as fine lines, dullness and uneven tone.

settings.title: Taspine
settings.text: An alkaloid unique to the resin, and the compound most associated with its wound-healing reputation. Research points to taspine supporting fibroblast activity - the skin cells responsible for repairing tissue.

settings.title: Phenols & flavonoids
settings.text: A broader phenolic profile rounds out the resin, contributing additional anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity alongside the proanthocyanidins.

settings.title: Forms a "second skin"
settings.text: On application it creates a breathable protective film that shields against the elements.

settings.title: Rich in antioxidants
settings.text: Naturally occurring flavonoids help defend skin against everyday oxidative stress.

settings.title: Supports collagen
settings.text: Studied for its role in supporting the collagen that keeps skin firm and smooth.

settings.title: Calms visible redness
settings.text: Known for its soothing effect on stressed, sensitised or irritated-looking skin.

settings.title: Locks in moisture
settings.text: Helps reduce water loss so skin stays hydrated and comfortable for longer.
